# Introduction
This vignette contains code and annotations to develop a package, to prepare for
package release, and to set up for a new version. It assumes the package has
been set up as described in the vignette *Package setup*:
[`utils::vignette("pkg_setup", package = "develcoder")`](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/pkg_setup.html).

# Adding functions
## Set up
```{r functions, eval = FALSE}
usethis::use_r("<func>")
devtools::document() # also runs devtools::load_all()
?<func>() # view help-page of the function
```

Do:

- Manually update the NEWS file:  
  `### Added functions`  
  ``- `<func>()` to ...``
- If the added function relies on other packages, update the dependencies given
  in the DESCRIPTION file: see section [Update dependencies].
- When adding a new function argument to an existing function, place the new
  argument after existing arguments and use a default value that matches the old
  behaviour: then code written for the old version will work the same as before
  the change even if it relies on positional matching, such that adding the new
  argument is a **non**-breaking change.
- When renaming a function, also change its name in the `_pkgdown.yml` file if
  that file is used to create a custom index for the website: all exported
  functions should be included in the function index and all functions included
  in the index should be exported functions, otherwise
  `pkgdown::build_reference()` will throw an error (`topic missing from index`
  or `must be a known topic name or alias`, respectively) and the package
  website cannot be build.

## Add documentation
Function files with file extension `.R` can be annotated using the 'roxygen'
format. Then use `devtools::document()`, which itself calls
`roxygen2::roxygenise()`, to create documentation files with file extension
`.Rd`.

The vignettes of [**roxygen2**](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/) describe many
aspects of package documentation, see
`utils::browseVignettes(package = "roxygen2")`,
among others vignettes with a general
[introduction to roxygen2](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/roxygen2.html)
and a general
[introduction to function documentation](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-functions.html).

Section titles [should](https://developer.r-project.org/Rds.html) be capitalized
and not end in a period. It is best to avoid all markup in titles because they
need to be automatically processed for various hypertext search systems. It is
possible to create
[subheadings](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-formatting.html#sections-and-subsections)
in roxygen blocks using `##` and `###`, i.e., usual Markdown syntax.

```{r documentation, eval = FALSE}
#' Title (should be capitalized and not end in a period)
#'
#' Description
#'
#' @param x Vector of names to test.
#' @param allow_NA `TRUE` or `FALSE`: allow [NA]s of the correct type in `x`?
#' @param x,y Separate arguments by a comma without a space to create a single
#' description for multiple arguments.
#'
#' @details
#'
#' @returns
#' `TRUE` or `FALSE`, returned [invisibly][invisible].
#'
#' @section Side effects:
#' The directory indicated by the returned path is
#' [created][progutils::create_dir()] if it does not yet exist.
#'
#' @section Notes:
#' Some notes.
#'
#' @section Programming notes:
#' Some programming notes. Create a GitHub issue instead of To do / Wishlist
#' sections.
#'
#' @seealso
#' Section `Details` of [make.names()] and the [\R FAQ about valid names](
#' https://CRAN.R-project.org/doc/manuals/R-FAQ.html#What-are-valid-names_003f)
#' on the syntactical validity of names.
#'
#' @family collections of checks on type and length
#'
#' @examples
#' all_names(x = c("a", "b2a")) # TRUE
#'
#' @export
func_name <- function(x, allow_NA = TRUE) {
  stopifnot(checkinput::is_logical(allow_NA))
  <...>
}
```

### Inherit documentation
It is possible to inherit sections of the documentation from other functions,
see the
[introduction to function documentation](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-functions.html)
from package **roxygen2**. Inherited sections are **silently** ignored if they are
also defined in the file itself.

Unfortunately, inheriting section `@seealso` does
[**not**](https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/issues/679) work if `@family` is
also used. Instead, hardcode the family members in the `@seealso` section of one
function and inherit that section in other functions using  
`#' @inherit fun seealso`.

``` {r inherit docs, eval = FALSE}
#' @inherit is_number return
#' @inherit is_number details
#' @inheritSection is_number Programming notes
#' @inheritSection is_number @details
```

### Inherit parameters
It is possible to inherit the description of parameters from other functions.
Since **roxygen2** 8.0.0, it is possible to specify which arguments to inherit
(i.e., to filter arguments). For arguments that share a single description, this
works from **roxygen2** 8.1.1.

``` {r inherit parameters, eval = FALSE}
# inherit the description for all arguments from a function in the current
# package (arguments that do not occur in the target function will be ignored)
#' @inheritParams diagnose_test_files pattern

# inherit the description for argument 'fields' from function
# 'installed.packages' in package 'utils'
#' @inheritParams utils::installed.packages fields
```

### Suppress documentation
Use the tag `@keywords internal` instead of `@export` to create an `.Rd` file
(and thus a help page) while omitting the function from the function index.
This is
[recommended](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/index-crossref.html#search)
for internal functions that are not supposed to be called by
the user. Use the tag `@noRd` instead of `@export` to not generate an `.Rd` file
at all (and thus omit the function from the index). In both cases, the function
is **not** exported and thus should be called using the triple-colon operator,
see `help(":::")`: `<pkg>:::<func>()`.

## Add examples
Examples are meant to show users how to use a function. Use
`devtools::run_examples()` to run all examples in a package.

Examples rendered on a website created with
[**pkgdown**](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/) will display the output underneath the
code. However, help files accessed through `help(<func>)` will not, such that it
might be useful to include a short comment regarding what feature of the output
is notable.

To not run or not display code in examples, you can use the `dontrun` and
`dontshow` tags, see `help("example", package = "utils")`, the section
[Examples](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Documenting-functions)
from the
[Writing R Extensions manual](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html)
and the section about 
[Examples](https://r-pkgs.org/man.html#sec-man-examples-errors) in the
'R packages' book.

Examples that create output files should write them to a temporary directory
that is cleaned up afterwards. See the section
[Usage in Practice](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/progutils/reference/create_tempdir.html#usage-in-practice)
in `help("create_tempdir", package = "progutils")` and section [Add tests] below.

## Add tests

### Background
For background on testing:

- Chapter [Unit tests](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/tests.html) from
  the [Bioconductor Packages](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/) guide
- [Testing basics](https://r-pkgs.org/testing-basics.html) and subsequent
  chapters from the 'R packages' book.
- [Code Testing](https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/testing/)
  and subsequent chapters.
- Section 'Packages tests' from the CRAN Task View
  [Package Development and Maintenance](https://cran.r-project.org/view=PackageDevelopment#packages-tests).

The code below shows how to run tests.

``` {r run-tests, eval = FALSE}
# Run all tests of a package. Use 'devtools::test()' instead of
# 'tinytest::test_all()' if you used package 'testthat' to create tests.
tinytest::test_all()

# Run a specific test file, selecting the file by name
tinytest::run_test_file(fs::path(getwd(), "inst", "tinytest", "test_funcname.R"))
```

### Expectations
Note that `tinytest::expect_silent(...)` tests that no errors or warnings are
emitted, **not** that no messages are emitted.

``` {r example-tests-tinytest, eval = FALSE}
expect_silent(expect_true(func_name(x = x, arg = arg)))
expect_warning(
  expect_equal(func_name(x = "a", arg = arg), 3),
  pattern = "...", strict = TRUE, fixed = TRUE)
expect_error(func_name(x = "a", arg = arg),
             pattern = "is_number(x) is not TRUE", fixed = TRUE)
```

### Interactive testing
To interactively run tests, attach the package that you want to test before
running the tests as explained in the previous paragraphs:

- use `devtools::load_all(<pkg>)` (with `unloadNamespace("develcoder")` to
  detach it)
- or use
  `attach(loadNamespace("<pkg>", versionCheck = list(op = ">=", version = package_version("1.2.3"))))`
  to specify which version to load, with `detach("<pkg>")` to detach it.

`pkgload::is_dev_package(<pkg>)` shows if a package was loaded through
`devtools::load_all(<pkg>)`, and `devtools::loaded_packages()` shows loaded
packages with the path from which they were loaded that can also be used to
identify development packages. See the section
[Loading and attaching packages](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/checkrpkgs/articles/r_pkgs.html#loading-and-attaching-packages)
in the vignette *R packages* from package **checkrpkgs** for details on loading
packages: `utils::vignette("r_pkgs", package = "checkrpkgs")`.

### Cleaning up
Tests that create output files should write them to a temporary directory
that is cleaned up afterwards. See the section
[Usage in Practice](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/progutils/reference/create_tempdir.html#usage-in-practice)
in `help("create_tempdir", package = "progutils")` and the
vignette [`test fixtures`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/test-fixtures.html)
from package **testthat** for more details. In addition, changed options
(`help("options", package = "base")`) and graphical parameters
(`help("par", package = "graphics")`) should be restored to their original state to
prevent
influencing subsequent code. The following pattern shows how to do so for a
single option or parameter, see
[this entry in the CRAN cookbook](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#change-of-options-graphical-parameters-and-working-directory)
for details:

```{r options, eval = FALSE}
orig_opt <- options(<option> = <value>)
orig_par <- graphics::par(<parameter> = <value>)
<code>
par(orig_par)
options(<option> = orig_opt)
```

To reset all parameters at once, use `orig_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)`. To
restore options that are changed inside a function, add `on.exit(par(orig_par))`
immediately after changing the option.

### Sorting order
Sorting order depends on the used locale, see 'Details' in `help("sort")`. For
example, sorting using the `C` locale gives the order
`c("-", "!", "_", "|", "=", "1", "a", "A")`, whereas sorting using `UTF-8` gives
`c("!", "-", "1", "=", "A", "_", "a", "|")`. Notably, the latter places
uppercase characters before instead of after lowercase characters and places
some symbols between the uppercase and lowercase characters, which also changes
the sorting order from `c("-", "_")` to `c("_", "-")`.

The used locale can be set through `Sys.getlocale()` but is also influenced by
the used operating system and other settings in `R`, see `help("locales")`,
section
[Locales](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Locales)
in the 'R Installation and Administration manual' and section 'Details' of
`help("Comparison")`. See the 'Programming Notes' in `checkinput::all_names()`
for more references.

### Testing file paths
Testing file paths requires some thought because the file separator depends on
the operating system (`.Platform$file.sep` gives the file separator on the
running platform) and the backslash is used as escape character in `R` such that
it needs to be escaped itself by doubling them. Thus, a check on the presence of
two successive slashes or backslashes in string `string` would use
`grepl(pattern = "//", x = string, fixed = TRUE)` and
`grepl(pattern = "\\\\", x = string, fixed = TRUE)`, respectively. The message
to point out their presence would be written as
`message("Successive '/' or '\\'")` which would be printed as
`Successive '/' or '\'`.

One approach to prevent problems with getting the correct type and number of
slashes to compare with the path recorded in a message is to check only for
fixed parts of the message (e.g., `"Successive"`), possibly followed by a check
like `tinytest::expect_true(fs::dir_exists(string))`.

## Update dependencies
First, consider if you really need a new dependency and which package that
should be. Some additional effort in choosing dependencies or in coding might
allow using dependencies that themselves have fewer dependencies, making a
project more stable over time. See the chapter
[Dependencies: Mindset and Background](https://r-pkgs.org/dependencies-mindset-background.html)
from the 'R packages' book for background, and its chapter
[Dependencies: In Practice](https://r-pkgs.org/dependencies-in-practice.html)
for practical advice.

### Check which packages are used
Package [**pkgstats**](https://docs.ropensci.org/pkgstats/reference/pkgstats.html)
can be used to check which packages, and which functions from those packages,
are used in your package. This requires the system libraries
[ctags-universal](https://ctags.io/) and
[GNU global](https://www.gnu.org/software/global/), which should be
automatically installed with **pkgstats** on Windows and MacOS. Use
`pkgstats::ctags_test(quiet = FALSE, noerror = TRUE)` to check if these are
indeed installed and `pkgstats::ctags_install()` to install them if not.

``` {r pkgstats, eval = FALSE}
if(requireNamespace("pkgstats", quietly = TRUE)) {
  overview_pkgstats <- pkgstats::pkgstats()
  overview_pkgstats$external_calls
}
```

Section
[Which packages are used](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/checkrpkgs/articles/r_pkgs.html#which-packages-are-used)
in vignette *R packages* from package **checkrpkgs** indicates how to manually
look for packages that are mentioned in comments:
`utils::vignette("r_pkgs", package = "checkrpkgs")`.

On **reverse** dependencies, see section [Check reverse dependencies].

### Importing packages or functions
The standard way to use functions from other packages is to import the package:
use `usethis::use_package(package = "<pkg>", type = "Imports", min_version = "<version>")`
to put the package in the `Imports:` field of the DESCRIPTION file. It is
possible to specify minimum package versions through argument `min_version`,
see [the next section][Specifying minimum versions].

``` {r imports-p1, eval = FALSE}
usethis::use_package(package = "checkinput", type = "Imports", min_version = "1.0.0")
```

If the package is only used in examples or vignettes, or is considered an
optional addition, you can use `type = "Suggests"` to place it in the
`Suggests:` field of the DESCRIPTION file. Code that uses that package should be
guarded through `if(requireNamespace(<pkg>, quietly = TRUE)) {<code>}`,
such that the code is only executed if the package is installed. This is not
necessary for the
['base' R packages](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html#Add_002don-packages-in-R)
that are always installed with R but **is** necessary for the
['recommended' packages](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html#Add_002don-packages-from-CRAN)
that are only automatically installed in binary installations and for all other
packages. From R 4.4.0, the names of the 'base' R packages and the 'recommended'
packages are available through `tools::standard_package_names()$base` and
`tools::standard_package_names()$recommended`, respectively.

Besides putting the package in the DESCRIPTION file, the package name should be
followed by two colons and the function name. For example, to use function
`all_names()`, first import package **checkinput** as described above and then
use  `checkinput::all_names()` in code. Specifying the appropriate package
through such notation is not possible if the function is an operator: then you
need to also list the **function** in the `NAMESPACE` file: use
`usethis::use_import_from(package = "<pkg>", fun = "<func>")` followed by
`devtools::document()` to add a line like `#' @importFrom utils ?` to the file
`R/<pkg>-package.R` that was created by `usethis::use_package_doc()`.
`usethis::use_import_from()` does not have a `min_version` argument, so to
specify one you have to use `usethis::use_package()` as described in the
next paragraph.

``` {r imports-p2, eval = FALSE}
# The first line is used to specify a minimum version
usethis::use_package(package = "utils", type = "Imports", min_version = "4.0.0")
usethis::use_import_from(package = "utils", fun = "?")
devtools::document()
```

### Specifying minimum versions
Specifying a minimum package version when importing packages ensures that used
functions are actually present. To use the currently installed package version,
use `usethis::use_package(package = <pkg>, <...>, min_version = TRUE)`. However,
that probably is
too strict because functions are likely also present in older package versions.

To check in which version a used functions was introduced, you can search the
NEWS file of the relevant package for the function name to find the NEWS
item announcing its introduction. If that does not work, you can search for the
function file on the GitHub-page of the package and look in its history to see
when it was created, or use the `Blame` feature to get a fine-grained overview
of when code in that file was changed to see when a function was introduced. Then
click on the commit message to get an overview of the files that were changed in
that commit and use the `Browse files` button to browse the repository as it was
repository as it was at the time of the commit. Then click the DESCRIPTION
file to see which version the package was in.
Finally, you can also specify different minimum package versions in checks
through [GitHub actions][Use GitHub Actions] and iteratively change them to
find the minimum version that passes the check. Then specify that version as
minimum version in your DESCRIPTION file.

Since R 4.6.0, `read.dcf()` recognises lines starting with `#` as comment lines,
making it possible to use comments in the DESCRIPTION file to indicate why a
particular package version is needed.

``` {r dependencies, eval = FALSE}
# Show the currently used R version
getRversion() # or: utils::packageVersion(pkg = "base")

# Declare a minimum version for R itself
usethis::use_package(package = "R", type = "Depends", min_version = "4.0.0")

# Declare a dependency on a package: 'use_package()' to declare a minimum
# version and 'use_dev_package()' to specify the remote repository to download
# the package from.
utils::packageVersion("checkinput")
usethis::use_package(package = "checkinput", type = "Imports", min_version = TRUE)
usethis::use_dev_package(package = "checkinput", type = "Imports",
                         remote = "github::JesseAlderliesten/checkinput")
utils::packageVersion("progutils")
usethis::use_package(package = "progutils", type = "Imports", min_version = TRUE)
usethis::use_dev_package(package = "progutils", type = "Imports",
                         remote = "github::JesseAlderliesten/progutils")
devtools::document()
```

Do:

- Add the minimum declared R version to workflows for
  [GitHub Actions][Use GitHub Actions].

# Adding vignettes
## Set up
``` {r vignettes, eval = FALSE}
usethis::use_vignette("my_vignette", title = "Some title")
# Add suggested dependencies on 'knitr' and 'rmarkdown'
usethis::use_package(package = "knitr", type = "Suggests")
usethis::use_package(package = "rmarkdown", type = "Suggests")
devtools::document()
pkgdown::build_article()
utils::browseVignettes(package = basename(getwd()))
```

If no vignettes are visible after running
`utils::browseVignettes(package = basename(getwd()))`,
probably `devtools::install()`
was run with the default argument `build_vignettes = FALSE`, use
`build_vignettes = TRUE` instead:  
`devtools::install(quick = FALSE, upgrade = FALSE, build_vignettes = TRUE)`. Run
`tools::pkgVignettes(package = "<pkg>")` for information about the vignettes
that R finds.

Use `utils::vignette("<vignette_title>")` (e.g., `utils::vignette("pkg_devel")`)
to render a vignette in the `help` pane of RStudio, and
`tools::Rd2txt("path/to/file.Rd")` to do so with an `Rd` file.

## Styling
See the vignette *R Markdown and knitr* on using R Markdown to style vignettes:
[`utils::vignette("rmarkdown_knitr", package = "develcoder")`](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/rmarkdown_knitr.html).

Put the next lines in the header of vignettes to get a table of contents:
``` {r vignette style, eval = FALSE}
output:
  rmarkdown::html_vignette:
  toc: true
toc_depth: 3
```

It is good practice to give the session information at the bottom of a vignette,
e.g., using `utils::sessionInfo()`, `sessioninfo::session_info()`, or
`sessioncheck::sessionstate()`:

```` {r session info, eval = FALSE}
## sessionInfo
```{r sessionInfo, echo = FALSE}
if(requireNamespace("utils", quietly = TRUE)) {
  utils::sessionInfo()
}
```
````

## Linking
- Link to another section in the same document:  
  `[<link text>][<Section title>]` or `[<Section title>]`.
- Link to a help page of a package:  
  `help("<func>", package = "<pkg>")` (unfortunately, `help("<pkg>::<func>")`
  does **not** work).
- Link from a help-page to a vignette:  
  ``The vignette *<vignette title>*: `utils::vignette("<vignette>", package = "<pkg>")` ``
- Link to another vignette in the same package:  
  `[<link text>](<vignette_filename>.html)`

There is [**no**](https://r-pkgs.org/vignettes.html#links) official way to link
from vignettes to help-pages or vice versa. **pkgdown** recognises calls like
`` `<func>()` `` and `` `<pkg>::<func>()` ``, such that relevant links for such
calls will be created on a package website. However, calls in which arguments
are supplied like `` `<pkg>::<func>(arg = x)` `` will not be linked, see the
[documentation](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/articles/linking.html) for details.

# Adding miscellaneous files
Non-standard files or folders should be added in the `inst` directory of the
package to pass [`R CMD check`](https://r-pkgs.org/R-CMD-check.html). Those
files and folders will be in the top-level package folder of the installed
package.

# Preparing for updates

## Check package name
Check if the correct package name is used in various files in the package
directory. The best way to ensure the correct package name is used is to use
dedicated functions to create the package structure and the relevant files,
e.g., `usethis::create_package()`, `cffr::cff_write(dependencies = FALSE)`,
`usethis::use_news_md()`, and `usethis::use_pkgdown()` instead of copying old
packages to start new packages.

``` {r pkg name, eval = FALSE}
devtools::document()
develcoder::pkg_name_correct()
```

## Check tests
Check if there are functions for which no test file was written and run all test
files. Use `devtools::test()` instead of `tinytest::test_all()` if you used
package [**testthat**](https://testthat.r-lib.org/) to create tests.

``` {r update tests, eval = FALSE}
devtools::document()
develcoder::check_tests()
# list with character(0) for elements 'missing' and 'extraneous' if all is fine
tinytest::test_all() # or devtools::test() if testthat was used to create tests
```

## Automated checks
The next sections provide code to run checks from various packages.

### Various packages
**BiocCheck** checks adherence to the
[`Bioconductor Packages`](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/) guide, which
is required before submission to [BioConductor](https://bioconductor.org/).
See the overview of checks in its
[vignette](https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc/vignettes/BiocCheck/inst/doc/BiocCheck.html).
Several of the checks are probably too strict if you do not intend to submit the
package to `BioConductor`.

[**checktor**](https://r-pkg.thecoatlessprofessor.com/checktor/) provides
various checks supplementing `R CMD check`.

``` {r checks-codetools, eval = FALSE}
devtools::load_all()

# This leaves a '<pkg>.BiocCheck' folder in the package repository:
BiocCheck::BiocCheck(package = getwd(), callr = requireNamespace("callr"))

# Return is invisible and silent if all is well
codetools::checkUsagePackage(
  pack = basename(getwd()), all = TRUE, suppressParamAssigns = TRUE)
checktor::checktor()
checktor::lab_description_function_quotes()
checktor::lab_format_names()
checktor::lab_title_starts_with_article()

# R cmd check also includes this check but it is faster to perform it beforehand
if(requireNamespace("tools", quietly = TRUE) &&
   utils::packageVersion("tools") >= "4.5.0") {
    tools::check_package_urls(dir = getwd(), verbose = TRUE)
}
```

### devtools (local)
[`devtools::check()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/check.html)
uses the preferred approach of first building the package before checking it.
[`rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck()`](https://rcmdcheck.r-lib.org/reference/rcmdcheck.html)
does not use that approach but can compare output from different checks.

See the [CRAN cookbook](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/) and
the appendix [R CMD check](https://r-pkgs.org/R-CMD-check.html) from the R
packages book on how to proceed if checks fail.

The call to `devtools::check()` used below is more strict than the default,
following suggestions from the
[Writing R extensions manual](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Suggested-packages)
and from [R packages](https://r-pkgs.org/release.html#double-r-cmd-checking) to
set arguments and
[environment values](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-ints.html):

- Using `TRUE` for environment variable `_R_CHECK_SUGGESTS_ONLY_` to run code
  while only using dependencies listed in the `Depends`, `Imports` and
  `Suggests` fields of the DESCRIPTION file.
- Using `TRUE` for environment variable `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_` to run code
  while only using dependencies listed in the `Depends` and `Imports` fields of
  the DESCRIPTION file. This catches cases where a package that is listed in
  the `Suggests` field of the DESCRIPTION file is used in a vignette without
  being run conditionally through `if(requireNamespace(<pkg>)) {<code>}`.
- Using `manual = TRUE` to build and check the manual.
- Using `remote = TRUE` (and thus `incoming = TRUE`) to run additional checks
  that are used by CRAN for new package submissions.

  These checks flag dependencies that are on GitHub, leading to `NOTE`s like  
  `Strong dependencies not in the CRAN or BioC software repositories: <pkg>`,  
  `Suggests or Enhances not in mainstream repositories: <pkg>`, and  
  `Unknown, possibly misspelled, fields in DESCRIPTION: 'Remotes'`.  
  You can ignore these `NOTE`s if you do **not** intend to submit to CRAN.
  
  These checks also identify problems with URLs that are used in the
  documentation. URLs:
  - should be accessible (e.g., point to public GitHub repositories, not to
    private repositories)
  - should be direct links, not redirects
  - should use the protocol `https://` instead of `http://`
  - should use the canonical forms expected by CRAN, not the 'simple' forms
    displayed in the webbrowser:
    - `https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=<pkg>` for packages
    - `https://CRAN.R-project.org/manuals.html` to refer to manuals
      [in general](https://CRAN.R-project.org/manuals.html) and URLs of the
      form `https://CRAN.R-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html` to
      refer to a
      [specific manual](https://CRAN.R-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html)
    - `https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/policies.html` to refer to the
      [CRAN policies](https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)
      (`R CMD check` will still complain about this format).
  
``` {r checks-devtools, eval = FALSE}
devtools::document()
devtools::release_checks()
if(utils::packageVersion("devtools") >= "2.5.0") {
  # check for missing `\value` and `\examples` fields in `Rd` files
  devtools::check_doc_fields()
}
devtools::check(manual = TRUE, remote = TRUE)
devtools::check(manual = TRUE, remote = TRUE,
                env_vars = c("_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_" = TRUE,
                             "_R_CHECK_SUGGESTS_ONLY_" = TRUE))
```

### goodpractice
Runs checks of its own and checks from various other packages.

``` {r checks-goodpractice, eval = FALSE}
# Select checks
# Show groups of checks: goodpractice::all_check_groups()
# Show all checks in some groups: goodpractice::checks_by_group(c("cyclocomp", "lintr"))
# Run all check from some groups:
# goodpractice::goodpractice(checks = goodpractice::checks_by_group(c("cyclocomp", "lintr")))
# Run all checks: goodpractice::goodpractice(checks = goodpractice::all_checks())
goodpractice_all_checks <- goodpractice::all_checks()
my_checks_goodpractice <- progutils::not_in(
  goodpractice_all_checks,
  c("covr", # time-consuming and wants 100% coverage
    "complexity_function_length", "cyclocomp", # I write complex functions
    # The lintr issue `Use == instead of %in% for scalar comparison` should be
    # ignored for 'x %in% y' if 'x' or 'y' might contain 'NA' that should be
    # removed: 'x %in% NA' and 'NA %in% y' return 'FALSE', whereas 'x == NA' and
    # 'NA == y' return 'NA'.
    "lintr_scalar_in_linter",
    "lintr_line_length_linter",
    "lintr_outer_negation_linter", # changes handling of NAs
    # flags data.frame() even if 'strings_as_factors' is not explicitly set
    "lintr_strings_as_factors_linter",
    "tidyverse_brace_linter",
    "tidyverse_function_left_parentheses_linter",
    "tidyverse_indentation_linter",
    "tidyverse_line_length_linter",
    "tidyverse_object_name_linter",
    "tidyverse_spaces_left_parentheses_linter",
    # does not find test files in inst/tinytest, use check_test_files() instead.
    "tidyverse_test_file_names",
    "tidyverse_whitespace_linter",
    # Checks similar to those from 'rcmdcheck' and 'urlchecker' are also used by
    # devtools::check() that already has been run above
    goodpractice_all_checks[
      grepl(pattern = "^rcmdcheck_|^urlchecker_", x = goodpractice_all_checks)]
  )
)

res_goodpractice <- goodpractice::goodpractice(
  path = ".", checks = my_checks_goodpractice)
res_goodpractice_failed <- goodpractice::failed_checks(res_goodpractice)
res_goodpractice_failed

# Can also show output of selected checks through
# res_goodpractice$checks$<check_name>
res_goodpractice
```

### Other checks
`devtools::check_win_release()` and `devtools::check_mac_release()` are similar
to `devtools::check()` and can be used to check packages on Windows or MacOS,
respectively. However, these checks might malfunction if your package has
dependencies that are not on CRAN or BioConductor. Such dependencies should have
been flagged above by `devtools::check(manual = TRUE, remote = TRUE)` as
`not in the CRAN or BioC software repositories` or as
`not in mainstream repositories`.

These checks email with a link to the webpage showing the check results if the
check is done, the webpage might display `504 Gateway Time-out` if the checks
have not finished yet.

``` {r checks-devtools-remote, eval = FALSE}
devtools::check_win_release()
devtools::check_mac_release()
```

### utils
Spell checking. This requires system libraries like [Aspell](http://aspell.net/).

``` {r checks-utils, eval = FALSE}
utils::aspell_package_Rd_files(dir = getwd())
utils::aspell_package_vignettes(dir = getwd())
```


## Update package-wide documentation

### DESCRIPTION
Run `desc::desc_normalize()` to normalize the DESCRIPTION file.

To show the DESCRIPTION file, use `desc::desc()` or
`utils::packageDescription(pkg = basename(getwd()))`. To only show the
dependencies, use `desc::desc_get_deps()` or
`utils::packageDescription(pkg = basename(getwd()), fields = c("Depends", "Imports", "Suggests", "Enhances"))`.

Manually increment the package version in the DESCRIPTION file, or use
`usethis::use_version()`. In the latter case, do **not** automatically `commit`
the change, but do so manually later on (i.e., choose a negative option when
presented with the question `Is it ok to commit them?`) to also commit the
updated CITATION, License, README and NEWS files.

See package
[**lifecycle**](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lifecycle) on how to add
badges to packages and functions to indicate their life cycle and its vignette
[Lifecycle stages](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html), chapter
[Lifecycle](https://r-pkgs.org/lifecycle.html) from the 'R packages' book, and
the [Semantic Versioning Specification](https://semver.org/) on versioning.

```{r description, eval = FALSE}
desc::desc_normalize()
# 'which' can be NULL, "major", "minor", "patch", or "dev"
usethis::use_version(which = NULL, push = FALSE)
```

### CITATION and License
Use the DESCRIPTION file to create a CITATION.cff citation file, or update
such file to reflect the new package version. Add a license if none is present,
or update it to have the correct year in it. **usethis** provides utility
functions to add licenses, see `help("licenses", package = "usethis")`. The code
below adds or updates a [MIT license](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/)
as an example.

```{r citation_license, eval = FALSE}
cffr::cff_write(dependencies = FALSE) # Create or update a citation file
usethis::use_mit_license()
```

### README
Install the development version of the package to ensure the updated version
number without Git-commit ID will be included in the citation format in the
README, using `quick = FALSE` and `build_vignettes = TRUE` to ensure the year
will be displayed:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
devtools::install(quick = FALSE, upgrade = FALSE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

Then `Knit` the README.Rmd to produce a README.md file. The citation in the
README should then display the updated version number.

Notes:

- The version badge at the top will still display the old version number, but
  that will change to the updated number when pushed to GitHub.
- If the requirement that README.Rmd and README.md are staged at the same time
  was accidentally introduced, delete the the hidden file
  `.git/hooks/pre-commit` from the R-project folder to remove that requirement,
  see the section 'DESCRIPTION' in
  `help("use_readme_rmd", package = "usethis")`.

### NEWS
Restyle the NEWS file and replace the heading `# <pkg> devel` with the version
number, e.g., `# develcoder 1.0.0`.

## Check reverse dependencies
**Acknowledgement**

This section reproduces a
[contribution](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2026q2/012397.html)
by Ivan Krylov to the
[R-pkg-devel mailing list](https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-package-devel)
of 26 May 2026.

To check if packages that use your package still pass their checks if you made
breaking changes, install the new version of your package, run
`tools::package_dependencies(reverse = TRUE, which = "most", recursive = "strong")`
to get the list of reverse dependencies, then use `utils::download.packages(...)`
to obtain their latest tarballs and finally run `tools::check_packages_in_dir()`
to check them.

`tools::package_dependencies()` and the related `tools::dependsOnPkgs()` only
take packages from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) into account.
`devtools::revdep(pkg = <your pkg>, bioconductor = TRUE)` also takes packages
from [BioConductor](https://bioconductor.org/) into account. To take other
non-CRAN packages into account, use
[`revdepcheck::revdep_check()`](https://revdepcheck.r-lib.org/reference/revdep_check.html)
or [`xfun::rev_check()`](https://pkg.yihui.org/xfun/manual#sec:man-rev_check)
(which has a [GitHub Action][Use GitHub Actions]:
[**crandalf**](https://github.com/yihui/crandalf)). If you find reverse
dependencies that broke because of your changes, use
`devtools::revdep_maintainers(pkg = <your pkg>)` to identify their maintainers
and then manually notify them.

## Locally test update
``` {r update, eval = FALSE}
devtools::document()
.libPaths() # Check if output of .libPaths() is correct.
# If the next line leads to the error 'lazy-load database
# '.../R/win-library/<X.Y>/<pkg>/R/<pkg>.rdb' is corrupt',
# you should restart R and again run the next line.
devtools::install(quick = FALSE, upgrade = FALSE, build_vignettes = TRUE)

# Load the package and view the help files as usual outside devtools:
library(basename(getwd()), character.only = TRUE)
utils::browseVignettes(package = basename(getwd()))
?progutils::reorder_levels
```

# Updating

## Use GitHub Actions
Set up `workflow_dispatch` to manually trigger 'GitHub Actions' ('GHA'), see the
section
[Automate checks](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/pkg_setup.html#automate-checks)
in the vignette *Package setup*:
`utils::vignette("pkg_setup", package = "develcoder")`.

To check if a reverse dependency (i.e., a package that depends on a package you
changed) **that you created** is still working fine: go to the `Actions` tab of
the reverse dependency, select the action you want to trigger (e.g.,
`check-standard.yaml`), and use the `Run workflow` button shown at the top of
the overview with workflow runs to run the `GitHub Action`. You can select which
branch it should run on but need to trigger it once manually on the `main`
branch to be able to trigger it manually on other branches.

Scheduled jobs that failed can be rerun through the button `Re-run jobs` >
`Re-run failed jobs` > `Re-run jobs`. If the `GitHub actions` page (e.g.,
https://github.com/JesseAlderliesten/develcoder/actions) indicates the package
passes [`R CMD check`](https://r-pkgs.org/R-CMD-check.html) whereas the badge on
the README indicates it fails, make sure `R CMD check` considers the `main`
branch (i.e., if the `devel` branch passes but the `main` branch fails, the
badge will have `failing`): use the `Run workflow` button to run the
`GitHub Action` on the `main` branch, see the previous paragraph.

If the package declares a dependency on a minimum R version, it is useful to
specify the minimum declared R version to run in addition to the ones that are
by default used in the template: for example, add
`- {os: ubuntu-latest, r: '4.1.0'}` to section `matrix: config:` to also run the
workflow with R 4.1.0 if your package declares R 4.1.0 as minimum version.

### GHA: documentation and help
For more background on 'GitHub Actions' ('GHA'), including an explanation of the
syntax used in `.yaml` files, see the section about
[GitHub Actions](https://r-pkgs.org/software-development-practices.html#sec-sw-dev-practices-gha)
in the 'R packages' book, the GitHub
[reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions)
and [How-to](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs),
and the section
[Automate checks](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/pkg_setup.html#automate-checks)
in the vignette *Package setup*:
`utils::vignette("pkg_setup", package = "develcoder")`, and the overview of
GitHub Actions and example Workflows in the documentation of the
[**actions**](https://github.com/r-lib/actions) package.

For help debugging build failures, see the Appendix
[R CMD check](https://r-pkgs.org/R-CMD-check.html) in the 'R packages' book and
the section
[Where to find help](https://github.com/r-lib/actions#where-to-find-help) in the
documentation of the [**actions**](https://github.com/r-lib/actions) package.

## pkgdown website
To automatically update the package website, one can use a
[GitHub Action][Use GitHub Actions] workflow (e.g.,
[`pkgdown.yaml`](https://github.com/JesseAlderliesten/develcoder/blob/main/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml))
that updates the website after a pull request or push. To set this up, run
`usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages()`.

To manually update the pkgdown website, use `pkgdown::build_site()` and open the
file `docs/index.html` in a web browser to preview the website, or look at the
files that constitute your package's website in the local `docs` directory.

See the documentation about package [**pkgdown**](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/)
and chapter [Website](https://r-pkgs.org/website.html) from the 'R packages'
book for further details.

### Styling
To customise the order in which the articles are listed, specify their order in
the `_pkgdown.yml` file: run `tools::pkgVignettes(package = "<pkg>")$names`
to get their names. See the
[**pkgdown** documentation](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/build_articles.html),
the `_pkgdown.yml`
[template](https://github.com/JesseAlderliesten/checkrpkgs/blob/main/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
from **develcoder**, and the non-alphabetical order of the
[articles](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/checkrpkgs/articles/) in the
**checkrpkgs** package for examples.

To create a custom function index (e.g., a thematic index instead of the default
alphabetically ordered one), include a section `reference:` in the
`_pkgdown.yml` file with the desired headings and topics: see the
[documentation](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/build_reference.html) and an
[example](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/main/pkgdown/_pkgdown.yml) from
[**pkgdown**](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/) and
[the `_pkgdown.yml` file from the **progutils** package](https://github.com/JesseAlderliesten/progutils/blob/main/_pkgdown.yml).
Then build the reference with `pkgdown::build_reference()` and view it locally
by opening the file `"<pkg>\docs\index.html"` and browse to 'Reference' to see
the package index.

## Committing
Commit the changes to the CITATION, License, README and NEWS files with the
commit message `Bump to version x.y.z`, to make it easier to find changes back
later on. `Pull` and `Push`.

## Merge devel-branch with main
To merge the `devel` branch with `main` (i.e., to incorporate the changes you
made to the `devel` branch in the `main` branch), go the the `devel` branch on
the GitHub website of the package. Then use `<Contribute>` > `Open Pull Request`
to do a pull request. Copy the updated section of the NEWS file in the
DESCRIPTION field to describe the changes, and put the package name with the
updated version number in the title of the pull request. Use the button
`Create pull request`.

If the message
`No conflicts with base branch: Merging can be performed automatically`, is
displayed, you can use the green `Merge pull request` button, or change to
`Squash and merge`.

Otherwise, the message `This branch has conflicts that must be resolved` will be
displayed: follow the instructions to resolve the conflicts. Then push the
button `Commit merge`. Then you should see `No conflicts with base branch` and
you can proceed as described in the previous paragraph.

After a successful merge, you will see a message that you can delete the
`devel`-branch, which you can do. To do so later, go to `Pull requests`, select
the `Closed` tab, and scroll down to the button `Delete branch`.

### Overwrite devel-branch after merge
In RStudio, open the relevant project to check there are no commits left. Then
you can move to the `main` branch and `Pull` to get all updates you just
committed to the `main` branch. Then click the `New branch` button in RStudio
(besides the `Switch branch` icon indicating which branch, e.g., `main` or
`devel`, you are using), use `devel` as branch name and click `Create`. You will
be notified that `devel` already exists and asked if you want to overwrite it.
**If** you have just merged `devel` into `main`, you can choose to overwrite
it to have a new `devel` branch.

### Set up a new branch
Instead of overwriting the `devel`-branch after merging into `main`, you can
also create a completely new branch:

- At the GitHub page of the package: `Branch` icon > green `New branch` button >
  specify a name for the branch > green `Create new branch` button.
- Go back to the GitHub page of the package, and at the green `Code` button >
  `copy URL to clipboard`.
- In RStudio: `File` > `New project` > `Version control` > `Git` and paste the
  copied URL in the `Repository URL` > `Create Project`.
- Then (still in RStudio) in the `Git` menu change from `main` to the
  just-created branch.

## Installing the updated package
Then you can delete the old package version from your PC (`find.package("<pkg>")`
gives its location) and install the updated version following your own
instructions on the GitHub pages of the relevant packages.

# CRAN submission
See the policy documents mentioned in the [Guidelines on package development]
and the chapter [Releasing to CRAN](https://r-pkgs.org/release.html) from the
'R packages' book.

`tools::CRAN_check_results()`, `tools::CRAN_check_details()` and
`tools::CRAN_check_issues()` give information about the current check status of
CRAN packages. [**cransays**](https://r-hub.github.io/cransays/index.html)
([source code](https://github.com/r-hub/cransays)) gives information about the
status of packages during package submission to CRAN.

# Troubleshooting
- If running checks lead to the warning
  `Warning in get_engine(options$engine): Unknown language engine '<name>' (must be registered via knit_engines$set())`,
  you probably forgot to indicate the knit-engine when naming a code chunk:
  ````
  `r ''````{use-sum}
  1 + 1
  ```
  ````
  erroneously tries to use the engine `use-sum`, whereas the probably intended
  `{r use-sum}` correctly indicates that the `r` engine should be used and the
  code chunk should be named `use-sum`:
  ````
  `r ''````{r use-sum}
  1 + 1
  ```
  ````
  See the output of `sort(names(knitr::knit_engines$get()))` for the available
  knit-engines.
- If running checks lead to the error
  ```
  `Failed with error: 'there is no package called '<pkg>''`
  `Quitting from <filename>.Rmd:<line numbers> [<chunk name>]`
  ```
  you probably
  forgot to use `library(<pkg>)` in a code chunck, used a package that is not
  declared as dependency in the DESCRIPTION file, or used a package that is
  declared as suggested dependency (i.e., is in the `Suggests` field of the
  DESCRIPTION file) without running that code conditionally on the presence
  of `<pkg>` through `if(requireNamespace(<pkg>)) {<code>}`. The latter is
  catched by using argument `env_vars = c("_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_" = TRUE)` when
  running `devtools::check()`.
- If checks fail because of LaTeX errors when building the manual, you can use
  `manual = FALSE`.
- If running `devtools::document()` leads to the error
  `@section Could not resolve link to topic ":blank:" in the dependencies or base packages`,
  `regex`-classes in example code are being interpreted as links. To prevent
  this, use backticks (`` ` ``) to format a line as code, or wrap consecutive
  lines in `\code{...}`.
- Errors can arise if package development is not done from a clean R session.
  Use `loadedNamespaces()` to check which packages are loaded, or use
  `utils::sessionInfo()`, `sessioninfo::session_info()`, or
  `sessioncheck::sessionstate()` for more information about loaded packages.
- See also section
  [Troubleshooting](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/checkrpkgs/articles/r_pkgs.html#troubleshooting)
  in the vignette *R packages* from package **checkrpkgs**:  
  `utils::vignette("r_pkgs", package = "checkrpkgs")`.
